newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up, local players take up positions.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up, local players take up positions.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Wednesday paring some of the market's losses Tuesday as local investors positioned themselves in stocks believed to have solid medium-term prospects, brokers said.
The market was likely to be broadly stable Thursday, they added.

According to preliminary figures given at the market's close Wednesday, the General Index IGRA rose 0.98 percent to 2,093.4 points, compared with a 2.51 percent fall Tuesday. The blue-chip Selective Index ISEL gained 1.13 percent to 3,016.6 points, compared to a 2.88 percent drop Tuesday.
In a total of 2,432 trades, volume was 36.0 million soles ($13.6 million), brokers said.

By late in the session, the enthusiasm from local players also attracted foreign funds to the market. Peru's largest brewery group Unin de Cerveceras Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA received most attention, gaining 2.38 percent to 2.58 soles on strong volume of 2.4 million shares.
"Today the market began a sustained recovery given that prices had experienced necessary technical corrections and had reached their floor," Manuel Bustamante of local brokerage Investa.
Benchmark Telefnica reversed early losses to end up 0.3 percent at 6.77 soles on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Financial holding company Credicorp -- the only blue chip to resist the undertow Tuesday -- continued its rise Wednesday, gaining 1.34 percent to close at $22.75 on volume of 10,400 shares.
